_: Continues where routes/opening.json ends: in Oak's Lab, starter in the party, rival battle won. Run both together — `--script` is repeatable, so this file never restates the opening. Its job is action balance: the opening is cutscene-heavy and harvests ~7 A-presses per move, while this leg is almost all walking plus whatever wild encounters Route 1 rolls.

Lab -> outside. The rival's post-battle speech is still on screen when the opening ends — its three trailing A-presses are a hand-count and they under-fire; measured, Red is still frozen behind ': Okay! Il make my...' and EVERY move returns BLOCKED. So do not lead with a goto here. Cycle [a, south] instead, the same idiom the opening uses to leave this room the first time: while the text runs the south is a no-op and the A advances it; once Red is free the A is harmless and the south walks him down column 5 to the door, which is a bottom-edge warp, so continuing south is also what steps out of it. Gate on the map id, never on {dialogue: false} — that is true for a frame between two boxes.
Pallet Town -> the Route 1 mouth at (10,1). The opening's goto to this same cell stops short because Oak intercepts; he is done now, so this one is expected to arrive.
North off the top edge of Pallet and into Route 1. A map boundary, not a warp — nothing appears in exits[] to aim at, so walk north until the map id says 12.

The length of Route 1, entering around (10,35) and climbing to its north edge. Named as one destination rather than a path: the route is fenced and hedged and the viewport shows ten blocks of it at a time, so the planner walks to the visible cell nearest the goal and looks again. Two gotos because MAX_LEGS bounds one of them, and the second is a no-op when the first arrives. This is the stretch that pays for the leg — it is grass the whole way, and do_goto fights the encounters it triggers rather than stalling on them.
Route 1 -> Viridian City, another map-boundary step.
Viridian City -> the Pokémon Centre door at (23,25), then one more north through the warp.

Up to the nurse's counter. A goto CANNOT be used in here: this interior decodes every walkable floor tile as '#', which navigate.py treats as a definite obstacle, so BFS finds no route and the planner refuses to move (Oak's lab decodes as '.', which is why the opening never hit this). Walking blind north is safe — the counter stops Red at y=3 — and `pos` is still a world fact rather than a press count.

Heal. The nurse's sequence is a greeting, a HEAL/CANCEL prompt that defaults to HEAL, and the machine animation — 13 A-presses when measured, and nothing guarantees that number. party_healthy watches the HP itself, which is the only fact the world exposes at the end of it. Full HP is also what makes this leg composable: the next one starts from a known state instead of whatever Route 1 left behind.
Back out into Viridian so the run does not end mid-textbox — the same handoff that broke the start of this file.
